en.bdb: Love between Sikh and the Guru

verses.gurmukhi: ਮਾਨ ਸਰੋਵਰੁ ਹੰਸਲਾ ਖਾਇ ਮਾਣਕ ਮੋਤੀ।
verses.translit_en: maan sarovar ha(n)salaa khai maanak motee|

en.bdb: The swan of Mansarovar picks up only pearls and jewels.

verses.gurmukhi: ਕੋਇਲ ਅੰਬ ਪਰੀਤਿ ਹੈ ਮਿਲ ਬੋਲ ਸਰੋਤੀ।
verses.translit_en: koil a(n)b pareet hai mil bol sarotee|

en.bdb: The nightingale and mango tree bear love for each other, and hence it sings thereupon.

verses.gurmukhi: ਚੰਦਨ ਵਾਸੁ ਵਣਾਸੁਪਤਿ ਹੋਇ ਪਾਸ ਖਲੋਤੀ।
verses.translit_en: cha(n)dhan vaas vanaasupat hoi paas khalotee|

en.bdb: The sandal loves whole vegetation, and whosoever is near it, becomes fragrant.

verses.gurmukhi: ਲੋਹਾ ਪਾਰਸਿ ਭੇਟਿਐ ਹੋਇ ਕੰਚਨ ਜੋਤੀ।
verses.translit_en: lohaa paaras bheTiaai hoi ka(n)chan jotee|

en.bdb: Touching the philosopher's stone the iron brightens like gold.

verses.gurmukhi: ਨਦੀਆ ਨਾਲੇ ਗੰਗ ਮਿਲਿ ਹੋਨਿ ਛੋਤ ਅਛੋਤੀ।
verses.translit_en: nadheeaa naale ga(n)g mil hon chhot achhotee|

en.bdb: Even the defiled streams, meeting the Ganges, become sacred.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪੀਰ ਮੁਰੀਦਾਂ ਪਿਰਹੜੀ ਇਹ ਖੇਪ ਸਓਤੀ ॥੬॥
verses.translit_en: peer mureedhaa(n) pirahaRee ieh khep sotee ||6||

en.bdb: Such is also the love between the Sikh and the Guru, and to a Sikh, this is most priceless commodity.
